sources.citation: Branchini, Chiara & Lara Mantovan (eds.). 2020. A Grammar of Italian Sign Language (LIS). Venezia: Edizioni Ca' Foscari. 830 pp. DOI 10.30687/978-88-6969-474-5 (CC BY 4.0).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent/'prominence' across all 831 pages: 7 hits for 'stress', none a placement statement (prosody chapter intro lists 'intonation, rhythm, stress, and prominence' as the domain of prosody; glossary defines syllable generically as 'the domain for stress assignment'; information-structure chapter uses 'stress' for focus emphasis via doubling). No word-stress rule anywhere in the grammar.

sources.citation: Mantovan, Lara. 2020. Part II Phonology, ch. 2 'Prosody', pp. 169-184 in Branchini, Chiara & Lara Mantovan (eds.), A Grammar of Italian Sign Language (LIS). (Lingue dei segni e sordità 1.) Venezia: Edizioni Ca' Foscari. DOI 10.30687/978-88-6969-474-5/010 (CC BY 4.0).

sources.note: Read in full. 2.1.1 Syllable: syllable = sequential movement; light (simple movement) vs heavy (complex movement) syllables; visual sonority hierarchy shoulder>elbow>wrist>base>non-base joints. 2.1.2 Foot: LIS signs tend to be disyllabic; inventories light+light, heavy+heavy, light+heavy, heavy+light patterns; only prominence statement is 'The variation between light and heavy syllables determines prominence in the signing flow.'
